q: The ____ around a charge Q are shown in Figure 9.9.
e: Equipotential surfaces are imaginary surfaces where every point has the same electric potential.

q: They are the ____ centred about the charge Q.
e: For a single point charge, the equipotential surfaces are concentric spheres.

q: The electric lines of force are radially outward and ____ to the equipotential surfaces.
e: Electric field lines always intersect equipotential surfaces at right angles.

q: The surface of a charged conducting sphere is an ____.
e: Since the electric field inside a conductor is zero and the surface charge is static, the entire surface is at the same potential.

q: This is because the charges, distributed uniformly on its surface, are ____.
e: In electrostatic equilibrium, charges on a conductor do not move, indicating no potential difference exists along the surface.

q: If the surface is not an equipotential surface, there will be the ____ and the charges would move from point to point.
e: A potential difference would create an electric field along the surface, causing charges to flow until equilibrium is reached.

q: The charged conductors may have any shape but their surfaces are all ____ as shown in Figure 9.10.
e: Regardless of shape, the outer surface of any charged conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is an equipotential surface.

q: In addition, the electric lines of force are ____ to the surface of the charged conductor.
e: If the field were not perpendicular, there would be a component of the field along the surface, causing charge movement.

q: The work done is ____ in bringing a charge from one point to another point on the equipotential surface.
e: Since the potential difference between any two points on an equipotential surface is zero, no work is required to move a charge along it.
